梅赛德斯车队负责人托托·沃尔夫表示，尽管意大利车手基米·安东内利拥有巨大的积分领先优势，但他仍必须警惕可能出现的意外"黑天鹅事件"使其冠军争夺战脱轨。
安东内利在蒙扎和马德里的背靠背胜利，使他对队友乔治·拉塞尔的冠军优势扩大到81分，本赛季还剩九站计划内的比赛。

尽管处于统治地位，安东内利最近多次强调，他驾驶时并没有想着世界冠军——他的车队负责人坚称这种态度是真实的。
"我向你保证他没有在想这件事，"沃尔夫说。
"这孩子能够如此区分开来，先做个年轻孩子，然后坐进车里成为成熟的赛车手。

"这就是为什么如果基米对自己说，'我没有在想冠军的事'，他就是没有在想冠军的事。
"我们也在努力，他的父母、我自己和车队都在说，这还没有结束。"
安东内利自3月29日赛季第三轮日本站夺冠后一直领跑积分榜，周日西班牙大奖赛后的81分优势是他本赛季保持的最大领先优势。
这位20岁车手的八场胜利比其他任何车手都多六场。
基米·安东内利在西班牙大奖赛首圈两次跑宽。
但沃尔夫表示，无论是车手还是车队都不能排除不可预测的情况。
"会有黑天鹅事件，它们可能发生，你会在你认为不可能失去的时候失去手中的东西，"梅赛德斯车队负责人补充道。
"我不想把事情搞复杂"——安东内利誓言保持专注
在马德里环道夺冠后，安东内利也强调还没有赢得任何东西。
"是的，这[积分领先]很棒，但我们只需要继续推进，继续交出成绩，每次上赛道都尽力做到最好，"他说。
"因为，当然，是的，我有很大的领先优势，但你永远不知道会发生什么。所以只需要为任何情况做好准备，继续最大化我得到的每一个机会，然后我们看看年底会走到哪里。"
基米·安东内利承认这不是他想要的获胜方式，并认为兰多·诺里斯配得上西班牙大奖赛的胜利。
这位20岁车手表示，他的支持网络，尤其是他的父亲马尔科，确保他保持脚踏实地和专注。
"我很幸运身边有非常好的人，"他补充道。
"我有一支不可思议的车队支持我，很棒的家庭。尤其是我爸爸，他是让我保持脚踏实地的人。
"有好人肯定帮助很大。是的，就这样。
"就我而言，正如我多次说过的，我只是努力在每场比赛中做到最好，每次坐进车里都尽可能开得快。然后我们看看年底会走到哪里。
"但我绝对不想把事情搞复杂，只是开车时担心冠军或结果。只是驾驶，做到最好。"

detailEn: Mercedes boss Toto Wolff issues Formula 1 title race caution despite Kimi Antonelli's big points lead

Kimi Antonelli's championship lead stands at 81 points after his Spanish GP victory with nine scheduled races to go this season; watch every session of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from September 24-26 with a Saturday race, live on Sky Sports F1
Sky Sports News' Craig Slater reflects on all the big talking points after a chaotic Spanish Grand Prix.
Mercedes boss Toto Wolff says Kimi Antonelli must remain wary about the potential of unexpected "black swan events" derailing his championship bid despite the Italian driver's large points lead.
Antonelli's back-to-back wins in Monza and Madrid have increased his championship advantage over team-mate George Russell to 81 points with a scheduled nine rounds remaining.
Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and McLaren's Lando Norris, third and fourth in the standings respectively, are now over 100 points behind.

Despite his dominant position, Antonelli has repeatedly stressed recently that he is driving without thinking about the world championship in mind - an approach that his team boss insists is genuine.
"I promise you he's not thinking about it," said Wolff.
"The way this kid is able to compartmentalise and be the young kid and then get into the car and be the mature racing driver.
Highlights from the 2026 Spanish Grand Prix.
"That's why if Kimi says to himself, 'I'm not thinking about the championship,' he's not thinking about the championship.
"And we are also trying, the parents and myself and the team, saying this is not finished."

Antonelli has led the championship ever since victory at the season's third round in Japan on March 29 with his 81-point advantage after Sunday's Spanish Grand Prix the largest he has held all season.
The 20-year-old's eight race wins are six more than any other driver.
Kimi Antonelli found himself going wide twice on the opening lap of the Spanish Grand Prix.
But Wolff says neither driver nor team can afford to rule out the unpredictable.
"There are black swan events, they can come and you're losing something out of your hand when you didn't think it was possible to lose," added the Mercedes team principal.
'I don't want to overcomplicate things' - Antonelli vows to stay focused
Speaking after victory at the Madring, Antonelli also stressed that nothing was won yet.
"Yeah, it [the points lead] is great, but we've just got to keep pushing, keep delivering the results and just trying to do the best job I can whenever I go on track," he said.

"Because, of course, yes, I have a big lead, but you never know what can happen. So just need to be ready for anything and keep maximising every opportunity I get, and then we'll see where we end up at the end of the year."
Kimi Antonelli admitted it wasn't the way he wanted to win and that Lando Norris deserved the Spanish GP victory.
The 20-year-old says his support network, particularly his father Marco, is ensuring he stays grounded and focused.
"I'm lucky to have really good people around me," he added.
"I have an incredible team that supports me, great family. Especially my dad is the one that keeps me on the ground.
"Definitely having good people helps a lot. And yeah, that's it.
"On my side, as I said many times, I just try to do my best every race, trying to really drive as fast as I can whenever I go in the car. And then we'll see where we end up at the end of the year.
"But definitely I don't want to overcomplicate things just drive worrying about championship or result. Just driving, doing my best."

detailEn: Qatar GP Qualifying: George Russell bounces back with superb performance to beat Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli to pole position

George Russell beats Kimi Antonelli to pole as Mercedes seal dominant one-two; Lando Norris ahead of Oscar Piastri on second row; Isack Hadjar beats Max Verstappen to fifth; watch the Qatar Grand Prix live on Sky Sports F1 at 4pm on Sunday, with build-up from 2.30pm
George Russell took pole position in Qatar as Kimi Antonelli seemed unhappy with his lap during qualifying
George Russell produced a superb performance in Qatar Grand Prix Qualifying to beat his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli to pole position.

The reignition of Russell's feud with Max Verstappen at last weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix had dominated the build-up to the penultimate race of the season, but the Brit produced the perfect response as he topped all three parts of qualifying.

That came as a surprise after Antonelli, who sealed the drivers' title with four rounds to spare, had topped all three practice sessions, but the Italian was unable to match Russell when it mattered most.

McLaren found significant improvement on the final runs to move ahead of Red Bull as Mercedes' nearest challenger and lock out the second row, with Lando Norris ahead of Oscar Piastri as the best of the rest despite being marginally either side of half a second down on Russell.
Verstappen, who said after winning in Las Vegas last weekend that Russell is "far below" his level, was beaten to fifth by his Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar.
Charles Leclerc took seventh but his Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton was beaten to eighth by Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad, with the latter's team-mate Liam Lawson completing the top ten.

George Russell says Lewis Hamilton is an equally 'ruthless competitor' to Max Verstappen but that his former team-mate has 'incredible values, grace and dignity'. Watch the full interview during Sky Sports F1's live Qatar GP coverage on Sunday
Kimi Antonelli outpaced Mercedes team-mate George Russell in final practice for the Qatar Grand Prix as the Silver Arrows continued to dominate.

Antonelli, who topped both of Friday's practice sessions, outpaced Russell by 0.249s and it looks highly likely a Mercedes driver will be on pole position after qualifying, which takes place later on Saturday at 6pm (build-up from 5.15pm), live on Sky Sports F1.
Mercedes appear to have a half-second advantage over the rest field as Max Verstappen was 0.510s adrift of Antonelli and the other Red Bull of Isack Hadjar was 0.687s behind.

Mercedes' dominance is a surprise as nearly every race following August's summer break has been very competitive at the front but it seems a combination of the smooth, high-speed track layout and Mercedes finally getting on top of their upgrades from a month ago has given them a significant margin on their rivals.
"Mercedes are almost in a class of their own, so it's worth the rest looking at the gap to Verstappen [in third]," said Sky Sports F1's Bernie Collins.

Ferrari had a difficult Friday after a spin for Charles Leclerc and an engine issue for Lewis Hamilton, but Leclerc fared better in final practice in fifth, ahead of McLaren's Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri.
Hamilton was unhappy throughout the session and stated his "car won't turn" after his final flying lap which put him in ninth, in between Racing Bulls duo Arvid Lindblad and Liam Lawson.
